nodes.label: LYNS Voice
nodes.rationale: Built as a native Tauri v2 app specifically to leave the browser-overlay era behind: no injecting into someone else's page, no browser speech-recognition lottery, no PowerShell or antivirus friction. Speech runs 100% on-device for zero cloud cost; Claude runs through the user's existing claude login.

nodes.label: Four reactive avatar states (Idle, Listening, Thinking, Speaking)
nodes.rationale: States are derived from real voice signals via a small host-neutral seam (VoiceSignals -> deriveState -> AvatarController) with fixed priority speaking > listening > thinking > idle, so any renderer can be driven unchanged. Activity owns motion; mood owns only a color tint on top (neutral is a pass-through for zero regression).
nodes.norm_label: four reactive avatar states (idle, listening, thinking, speaking)

nodes.label: Mood tag convention (<<mood:NAME>>)
nodes.rationale: The marker is always stripped before TTS and captioning so a stray tag is silently removed rather than spoken; no tag keeps the orb neutral, guaranteeing zero regression when Claude does not cooperate.

nodes.label: Oracle wake word
nodes.rationale: Entirely on-device with no egress; while enabled the mic stays open locally to hear the phrase, so a turn can start without a tap. Optional, because the always-open mic is a deliberate privacy trade-off.

nodes.label: Kokoro neural TTS (in-process)
nodes.rationale: Runs in-process via ort/ONNX Runtime with misaki-rs g2p, replacing the old PowerShell-spawning path that hit antivirus friction; speech synthesizes to a WAV buffer played through Web Audio so real amplitude drives the Speaking animation. Native Windows SAPI remains a settings toggle that skips the ONNX Runtime memory cost.

nodes.label: Local Whisper STT with VAD endpointing
nodes.rationale: whisper-rs plus webrtc-vad endpointing lets an utterance auto-finalize on a pause (hands-free auto-send), genuinely offline; the model downloads once on first run with resumable transfer, progress, and ETA.
nodes.norm_label: local whisper stt with vad endpointing

nodes.label: Claude CLI stream-json sidecar bridge
nodes.rationale: Rust drives the claude CLI as a long-lived sidecar (--print --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json), parsing NDJSON events into avatar states and telemetry. Sessions are keyed by id so several run in parallel, each with its own --model/--effort, and a turn is cancellable mid-flight for barge-in.

nodes.label: Holographic orb centerpiece
nodes.rationale: A vendored, self-contained MIT Three.js renderer wrapped by a thin adapter, so the four-state controller, mood layer, and voice loop drive it with zero controller changes.

nodes.label: The conductor (multi-session orchestration)
nodes.rationale: The primary voice session spawns and steers background Claude Code sessions with courteous voice arbitration, propose-before-fan-out approval, spawn gating to the project directory, and fleet cost telemetry, keeping human oversight of fan-out.

nodes.label: The Library (MCP servers and hooks panel)
nodes.rationale: LYNS Voice inherits the MCP servers and hooks the user already configured for Claude Code, each visible and one-click toggleable per new session, so the user's own terminal registration remains the consent boundary.
nodes.norm_label: the library (mcp servers and hooks panel)

nodes.label: Per-tool permission cards: verified-not-shipped
nodes.rationale: The claude CLI exposes no --permission-prompt-tool and --permission-mode default emits no answerable event in headless stream-json, so per-tool read-and-click approval cards would require migrating to the Claude Agent SDK (out of scope). The allowlist + per-tool visibility + barge-in remain the HITL surface. Verified, not assumed.

nodes.label: dontAsk allowlist capability surface
nodes.rationale: dontAsk is non-interactive (the headless sidecar can never hang on a dialog) AND denies any tool not on the allowlist, making the allowlist the entire auditable capability surface. Never bypassPermissions. The denylist is best-effort pattern-match defense-in-depth against catastrophic shell commands, explicitly not a sandbox.

nodes.label: Project-directory blast radius
nodes.rationale: Each Claude session requires a project directory as its working directory; that directory is the intended blast radius (defense-in-depth, not an OS sandbox). Sessions live in a per-id map so each is scoped to its own directory.

nodes.label: MCP inheritance (terminal MCP world)
nodes.rationale: User-scope MCP servers are allowlisted for every session because the user's registration is the consent boundary, exactly as in the terminal. Project-scope .mcp.json servers are deliberately NOT auto-allowed (they can arrive inside a cloned repo, and LYNS Voice must not be more permissive than the user's own terminal). Under dontAsk there is no per-call prompt, so write-capable servers run unconfirmed; every call is visible live and the Library offers per-server off switches.

nodes.label: Hooks inheritance and per-session override
nodes.rationale: The user's configured Claude Code hooks run inside LYNS Voice sessions exactly as in the terminal (--print executes them); the Library can disable any hook per new session via a per-session --settings override so the user's files are never modified. Editing a hook changes its Library id, naturally re-enabling it.

nodes.label: Strict CSP and egress policy
nodes.rationale: No remote origins; the only egress is the claude child and the one-time speech-model downloads done in Rust, which are SHA-256 checksummed and size-capped with HTTP-range resume. Wake-word audio never leaves the device because the CSP allows it nowhere to go.

nodes.label: Human-in-the-loop model (visibility + interrupt)
nodes.rationale: Every tool streams live to the session panel and Activity feed; Escape (or voice barge-in) interrupts an in-flight turn at any time; the mic is never load-bearing because typed input is a co-equal path. Per-tool approve/deny cards were verified impossible with claude 2.1.183 headless stream-json, so allowlist + visibility + interrupt is the shipped HITL surface.

nodes.label: User-owned ConPTY shell
nodes.rationale: The spawnable terminals run with the user's authority, not Claude's, and are not driven by any Claude session: the escape hatch for what Claude cannot or should not do. The allowlist constrains Claude, not the user.

nodes.label: AVATAR_SPEC: real-time 3D desktop avatar overlay specification
nodes.rationale: Original blueprint from the retired mcp-voice-hooks browser-overlay era; audio processing had to run 100% locally via the browser Web Speech API to ensure zero additional API cost while keeping Claude Max reasoning. Only its four-state behavior rules survive as the behavioral source of truth.
nodes.norm_label: avatar_spec: real-time 3d desktop avatar overlay specification

nodes.label: Expected behavior rules for the four avatar states
nodes.norm_label: expected behavior rules for the four avatar states

nodes.label: Permissive-only license policy
nodes.rationale: Every third-party component must be under a permissive MIT-compatible license; no GPL, LGPL-only, or AGPL code is included. Where a license requires preserved attribution (CC-BY-3.0, Apache-2.0, MPL-2.0) the notice carries it. r-efi is used under its MIT/Apache option, not LGPL.

nodes.label: Whisper STT model ggml-base.en-q5_1 (MIT)
nodes.rationale: Downloaded once on first use from Hugging Face (ggerganov/whisper.cpp) and verified by a pinned SHA-256 before use; the exact URL and checksum live in src-tauri/src/stt.rs.

nodes.label: Kokoro-82M TTS model and voices (Apache-2.0)
nodes.author: hexgrad and the onnx-community contributors
nodes.rationale: model_fp16.onnx is verified by a pinned SHA-256 before use; vocab/config and voice packs are HTTPS-fetched and size-capped. Checksums live in src-tauri/src/kokoro.rs.

nodes.label: misaki-rs with espeak feature off
nodes.rationale: misaki-rs is built with default-features = false so its optional espeak (GPL) backend is NOT compiled in, preserving the permissive-only dependency tree; out-of-vocabulary words fall back to letter spelling.

nodes.label: vendor/head.glb default avatar head
nodes.author: Lee Perry-Smith / Infinite Realities
nodes.rationale: Committed so the avatar runs 100% locally with no runtime CDN fetch; a realistic head used as a proven default for the loader pipeline, swappable at runtime via the headUrl config field for any uncompressed non-Draco GLB without code changes.

nodes.label: Spike A: bloom vs transparent canvas (FAILED)
nodes.rationale: At Three.js r128, EffectComposer + UnrealBloomPass turned the canvas opaque black even with the alpha-safe pass chain (verified in headless Chromium over a magenta backdrop): r128 postprocessing assumes an opaque screen clear, so composer bloom cannot be the transparent-overlay glow. The bloom experiment was reverted and the halo shell shipped instead.
nodes.norm_label: spike a: bloom vs transparent canvas (failed)

nodes.label: Halo shell (BackSide additive fresnel glow)
nodes.rationale: A slightly enlarged BackSide additive fresnel shell (HALO_FRAGMENT_SHADER + Avatar.syncHalo) gives a soft volumetric rim glow while, being ordinary geometry, preserving canvas transparency; combined with fresnel + CSS drop-shadow it matches the reference look.

nodes.label: Spike B: mood-tag reliability (PENDING)
nodes.rationale: The parser is tolerant (tag anywhere in the first ~40 chars, case-insensitive, length-capped) and ALWAYS strips, so a stray tag is silent; with zero tags the avatar stays neutral (zero regression). Behavioral reliability of Claude emitting the tag is validated live; if unreliable, keep best-effort + neutral default and consider a deferred set_avatar_mood helper.

nodes.label: postcss bump 8.5.15 -> 8.5.26
nodes.rationale: Fixes GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849 (high, path traversal via sourceMappingURL leading to arbitrary .map disclosure) and its incomplete-fix follow-up GHSA-fxqj-rqcc-2cmp (medium); dev-scope transitive dep of vite, fixed by lockfile bump.

nodes.label: brace-expansion bump 5.0.6 -> 5.0.9
nodes.rationale: Fixes GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp (high): denial of service via exponential-time expansion of consecutive non-expanding {} groups; transitive dep of eslint via minimatch.

nodes.label: glib 0.18.5 advisory dismissed as not-used
nodes.rationale: glib is pinned by the gtk 0.18 stack Tauri v2 requires (no patched upgrade path until Tauri migrates to gtk-rs 0.20); it is Linux-target-only while LYNS Voice ships Windows-only, so it is never compiled into the released binary; and the advisory is memory unsoundness in an iterator impl, not remotely reachable. Revisit on the next Tauri bump.

nodes.label: CI build job (lint, typecheck, unit, build, e2e)
nodes.rationale: Uses npm install rather than npm ci: the lockfile is generated on Windows, but the Vite 8 native toolchain (rolldown/oxc -> @napi-rs/wasm-runtime -> @emnapi/*) resolves a wasm fallback on Linux that Windows never installs, so a Windows-authored lockfile cannot satisfy strict npm ci on Linux; npm install reconciles per-platform.
nodes.norm_label: ci build job (lint, typecheck, unit, build, e2e)

nodes.label: CI rust job (cargo test --lib)
nodes.rationale: Installs webkit2gtk 4.1 (the Tauri 2 webview), libclang-dev (whisper-rs bindgen), and cmake (whisper-rs-sys); compiles the Tauri app crate so Rust regressions are caught in CI, running only hermetic unit tests (model/engine-driven tests are #[ignore]).

nodes.label: CI security job (npm audit, cargo audit, gitleaks)
nodes.rationale: Dependency audits are informational (continue-on-error, advisories the owner can triage) while the gitleaks secret scan is blocking (secrets must never land). gitleaks needs fetch-depth: 0 (it scans the pushed commit range, not a shallow clone) and pull-requests: read on PR events (it lists PR commits via the API; without it the default token 403s).
nodes.norm_label: ci security job (npm audit, cargo audit, gitleaks)

nodes.label: CodeQL analyze job (javascript-typescript)
nodes.rationale: Runs weekly on cron so newly-disclosed patterns get caught even without a push. The upload step is continue-on-error because result upload requires code scanning enabled on the repo (GitHub Advanced Security for private repos); the analysis still runs each push, and enabling code scanning in Settings turns alerts on with no workflow change.

nodes.label: Issue template contact links (discussions + private security advisories)
nodes.rationale: blank_issues_enabled is false so all reports route through structured forms; security vulnerabilities are routed to private GitHub Security Advisories, never public issues.
nodes.norm_label: issue template contact links (discussions + private security advisories)

nodes.label: Desktop app shell HTML (HUD, settings drawer, stage, caption)
nodes.rationale: The center column of the three-column stage is intentionally empty so the full-window orb shows through with side panels floating over its glow; the spoken-reply caption exists to keep replies readable even when audio is off, with mood markers stripped before they reach it; the TAP TO TALK footer button proxies the same listening logic as the mic button, wired together in main.ts.
nodes.norm_label: desktop app shell html (hud, settings drawer, stage, caption)

nodes.label: Host-free demo harness HTML
nodes.rationale: A control panel drives the four avatar states directly (idle/listening/thinking/speaking buttons) plus real mic and speech tests, so the avatar can be exercised in a browser with no Tauri host or backend.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md project instructions (LYNS Voice)
nodes.rationale: Working agreement: answer open implementation questions as the senior engineer and record rationale; clean code, security first, tests baked in as built; phased delivery with a green gate between phases; no em or en dashes in generated content; tune visuals against a concrete target one knob per turn because open-ended visual trial-and-error burns tokens.
